_meta.rule: E-first identity: delivery side from autoattack range (>= 9 ranged) or the E damage's own reach (flex); damage scale from the E's burst_aoe claim; healers/frontline/support style-flexible; trio fits everything; style_overrides.yaml wins with citation. DESCRIPTIVE - no scoring path reads this.

override.reason: Owner ruling (round 7, refining the 2026-08-23 situational grade): "spirithunter is great in clap and clap kite, just read the e ability, it has a massive pierce that enables the whole dps line." The dump text agrees: Corrupting Steel pierces THROUGH all enemies, cuts damage resistances of every enemy hit, and its trail cuts magical resistance further — the pierce lens's own capability, delivered line-wide. The derivation grades the weapon single-scale because the E's damage (80) is incidental; the E's JOB is the Pierce stage of the CLAP chain (engage-clump-pierce-burst), so clap and its clap_kite hybrid take it as a fit. Brawl/kite keep the derived situational grade — the killboard fields it inside the brawl-ball family too (68% of F1's cohorts), but the owner promoted only the clap halves.

Owner ruling (forge-quality blind round): "great holy is not a good fit for clap, it has to stop moving and needs everyone to clump in place to heal with e. that's not good" and "great holy I feel isn't really that good of a weapon in general but I only see it being useful in like brawl situations." The derivation grades healers style-flexible; the E-first rule overrules that here — Holy Explosion anchors the party in place, the opposite of what clap's engage-bomb-reset and kite's never-take-the-fight delivery need. Brawl (and brawl_clap's grind half) keep it; trio bands gate nothing by the standing Phase C rule.

Owner ruling (forge-quality round 4): "flex bomber like hellfire, it's usually a brawl-clap weapon and not a clap option. realmbreaker gives multiple things like health cut, range e, easy way to engage followup — that's why it can work in clap." The flex all-rounder derivation grades both as clap-fits; the owner splits them: Hellfire's Boulder Toss is a brawler's ranged tool, not a clap bomb core, so clap drops to situational (the generation-fit gate then keeps it out of DEFAULT clap comps while brawl-clap — its home — keeps it, and a caller can always pick it manually). Realmbreaker stays as derived.

Owner ruling (round 7): "hellspawn staff is another staff which is primarily single target damage and therefore not good in above 5 member parties normally." The E is the Hellfire Imp transformation (self-target, very high single-target offense) — the form's damage is solo-target; the derivation had graded the weapon group-scale through its sheet caps.

Owner ruling (round 7 E-audit follow-up): "trinity spear seems like a group tool but no one is doing auto attack damage usually so its never used in large scale. only time its used is for a swap for hitting castle gates or terry walls. to get the attack speed and start taking walls faster.. but never as the main weapon in party." The E derives group-fits (root-all + area impact + ally mist), but its headline buff is an AUTO-ATTACK steroid — worthless in large fights where nobody auto-attacks; the real large-scale use is a structure-siege weapon SWAP, not a comp slot. Gang keeps the derived verdict (the ruling names large scale only); manual picks score as always.

Owner ruling (round 7, observed-family reconciliation): "warbow on the other hand would be terrible in a group setting because its e is single target damage and it can get easily blocked." The derivation read Magic Arrow's max_targets 5 as group-scale, but its footprint is a 3.0 x 2.5 line — in practice the first body eats it, exactly the blockable solo-arrow class the owner names. The E-first rule stands: max effective at 3, okay at 5, falls off hard beyond.

Owner ruling (V3-adjacent identity session): "although it's an axe and provides healthcut and possibilities for mobility on its w spell, it doesn't fit in most group play styles bigger than 3 because its e spell, the primary identity, doesn't do as much damage as other options for a group setting (5+)." The derivation reads its utility points (catch, engage, healthcut, root) as exempting it to 'situational'; the E-first identity rule overrules that — Axe Throw (burst_st 2, radius 1.5) is not a group damage tool, and the utility pieces do not carry a group slot on their own.

Owner ruling (round 7): "any primarily solo target abilities, like dagger pair 1 hand fire etc are max affective in 3 man situations and then good/okay at 5 man and then start falling off hard if party grows." Pyroblast is a channeled projectile that detonates on the FIRST enemy hit (dump text: "upon impact with an enemy") — a blockable solo nuke the derivation graded group-scale from its impact radius.
